    // True when every pair of corresponding components differs by no more than
    // the given (non-negative) tolerance.
    AlmostEqual(a: IVector, b: IVector, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => a.AllZipComponents(b, (x, y) => x.AlmostEqual(y, tolerance));

    // True when every component is within the given tolerance of zero.
    AlmostZero(self: IVector, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => self.AllComponents(x => x.AlmostZero(tolerance));

    // True when every component lies in the inclusive box [lower, upper].
    Between(self: IVector, lower: IVector, upper: IVector): Boolean
        => self.AllZipComponents(lower, upper, (x, a, b) => x.Between(a, b));

    // True when every component is finite (no infinity, no NaN).
    IsFinite(self: IVector): Boolean
        => self.AllComponents(x => x.IsFinite);

    // True when at least one component is NaN.
    HasNaN(self: IVector): Boolean
        => self.AnyComponent(x => x.IsNaN);

    //==
    // # Numeric structures components — the IVector component surface
    //
    // The map/zip/fold combinators over a vector's components, the reductions built
    // on them (SumComponents, Magnitude, Dot), the distinguished elements derived
    // from Broadcast, and the per-concrete-type FromComponents/Broadcast primitives
    // that close the loop. Everything here is written once and applies to every
    // IVector implementor.

    //==
    // # IVector â€” component-wise lifting
    //
    // IVector declares FromComponents and Broadcast and inherits Count/At from
    // IIndexable<Number>, so a vector can be both read as and rebuilt from an
    // Array<Number>. That closes the loop: the Array intrinsics (Map, Zip,
    // Reduce, All, Any) lift straight onto vectors, and every derived body below
    // is written once instead of once per concrete type.
    //
    // As elsewhere in these libraries, the helpers return the bare interface type
    // IVector rather than the concrete implementing type.

    // The components of self as an Array<Number>, in index order.
    ComponentArray(self: IVector): Array<Number>
        => self.Count.Range.Map(i => self[i]);

    // A vector of the same type with f applied to each component.
    MapComponents(self: IVector, f: Function1<Number, Number>): IVector
        => self.FromComponents(self.ComponentArray.Map(f));

    // A vector whose i-th component is f applied to the i-th components of a and
    // b. Precondition: a and b have the same arity.
    ZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, f: Function2<Number, Number, Number>): IVector
        => a.FromComponents(a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, f));

    // The three-way component-wise zip. Precondition: equal arities.
    ZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, c: IVector, f: Function3<Number, Number, Number, Number>): IVector
        => a.FromComponents(a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, c.ComponentArray, f));

    // Folds the components left to right, starting from initial.
    ReduceComponents(self: IVector, initial: Number, f: Function2<Number, Number, Number>): Number
        => self.ComponentArray.Reduce(initial, f);

    // True when every component satisfies the predicate.
    AllComponents(self: IVector, predicate: Function1<Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => self.ComponentArray.All(predicate);

    // True when at least one component satisfies the predicate.
    AnyComponent(self: IVector, predicate: Function1<Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => self.ComponentArray.Any(predicate);

    // True when the paired components of a and b all satisfy the predicate.
    AllZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, f: Function2<Number, Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, f).All(x => x);

    // True when the tripled components of a, b and c all satisfy the predicate.
    AllZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, c: IVector, f: Function3<Number, Number, Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, c.ComponentArray, f).All(x => x);

    // True when at least one paired component of a and b satisfies the predicate.
    AnyZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, f: Function2<Number, Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, f).Any(x => x);

    // True when at least one tripled component of a, b and c satisfies the predicate.
    AnyZipComponents(a: IVector, b: IVector, c: IVector, f: Function3<Number, Number, Number, Boolean>): Boolean
        => a.ComponentArray.Zip(b.ComponentArray, c.ComponentArray, f).Any(x => x);

    //==
    // # IVector â€” component reductions

    // The sum of all components.
    SumComponents(self: IVector): Number
        => self.ReduceComponents(0.0, (acc, x) => acc + x);

    // The sum of the squares of all components; the squared Euclidean norm.
    SumSqrComponents(self: IVector): Number
        => self.ReduceComponents(0.0, (acc, x) => acc + x * x);

    // The smallest component. Precondition: the vector has at least one component.
    MinComponent(self: IVector): Number
        => self.ReduceComponents(self[0], (acc, x) => acc.Min(x));

    // The largest component. Precondition: the vector has at least one component.
    MaxComponent(self: IVector): Number
        => self.ReduceComponents(self[0], (acc, x) => acc.Max(x));

    // The arithmetic mean of the components. Precondition: non-empty.
    AvgComponent(self: IVector): Number
        => self.SumComponents / self.Count.ToNumber;

    // The Euclidean length (the INormed member, derived from the components).
    Magnitude(self: IVector): Number
        => self.MagnitudeSquared.Sqrt;

    // The squared Euclidean length; avoids the square root.
    MagnitudeSquared(self: IVector): Number
        => self.SumSqrComponents;

    // The dot product: the sum of the products of corresponding components.
    // Precondition: a and b have the same arity.
    Dot(a: IVector, b: IVector): Number
        => a.ZipComponents(b, (x, y) => x * y).SumComponents;

    //==
    // # IVector â€” distinguished elements
    //
    // The INumericalLimits surface follows from Broadcast alone: each element is
    // the corresponding Number constant in every component.

    // The vector with every component zero (the additive identity).
    Zero(self: IVector): IVector
        => self.Broadcast(0.0);

    // The vector with every component one.
    One(self: IVector): IVector
        => self.Broadcast(1.0);

    // The vector with every component at the smallest representable Number.
    MinValue(self: IVector): IVector
        => self.Broadcast(Number.MinValue);

    // The vector with every component at the largest representable Number.
    MaxValue(self: IVector): IVector
        => self.Broadcast(Number.MaxValue);

    //==
    // # IVector construction, per concrete type
    //
    // FromComponents and Broadcast are the only primitives the generic bodies
    // above need; each implementing type supplies them once here through its
    // synthesized constructor. Everything else in this section is derived.

    // The 2-tuple built from the first two entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Number2, xs: Array<Number>): Number2
        => (xs[0], xs[1]);

    // The 2-tuple with both components set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Number2, x: Number): Number2
        => (x, x);
